sources.title: Cognitive Interviewing
sources.organization: CDC National Center for Health Statistics, CCQDER
sources.locator: Characteristics; Follow-up questions; Findings; Analysis and five levels of analysis
authorized_claims: cognitive interviewing examines how respondents understand and answer questions
purposive selection is appropriate when the objective is problem detection rather than population estimation
probes can examine comprehension, recall, judgment and response selection
sources.limitations: Guidance concerns question evaluation generally; it does not validate CitoNauta items, determine universal sample sizes for this pilot or replace local ethical requirements.

sources.title: Appendix A2: Questionnaire Testing and Evaluation Methods for Censuses and Surveys
sources.locator: Cognitive interviews and respondent debriefing sections
authorized_claims: respondent debriefing can test whether intended concepts and questions are understood as designed
debriefing can help identify sources of misunderstanding and needed revisions
sources.limitations: The document is a federal survey quality standard, not a course-validation standard and not evidence that the current educational material has already been tested.

sources.title: A Coefficient of Agreement for Nominal Scales
authorized_claims: Cohen's kappa represents chance-corrected agreement for two raters assigning nominal categories
binary critical-error flags can be summarized with unweighted kappa when expected agreement does not make the coefficient undefined
sources.limitations: Kappa is sensitive to marginal distributions and does not replace the raw agreement table or substantive examination of disagreements.

sources.title: Weighted kappa: Nominal scale agreement provision for scaled disagreement or partial credit
authorized_claims: weighted kappa permits disagreements to receive different weights
an ordinal 0–2 rubric can use declared linear weights when adjacent disagreements should count less than extreme disagreements
sources.limitations: The choice of weights is an analytical decision. The metric does not establish content validity, reviewer competence or adequacy of the rubric by itself.
